result.reason: Both items are part of the continuous Gemara discussion about what Chizkiya means when he says 'a bird has no lungs,' which is precisely what candidate 7 ('Lungs protected by ribs') describes in its prose — the challenge that birds visibly have lungs, the attempted reinterpretation that lung-tereifot don't apply, the refutation from Levi's teaching, and the final resolution that Chizkiya means the lung need not be checked for falling or singeing because the ribs protect it.

The passage contains precisely the content described in candidate 0's prose: the Gemara's inference that Chizkiya held birds have no lungs, followed by the Western tradition in Rabbi Yosei b'Rabbi Chanina's name declaring Chizkiya simply unfamiliar with chickens — which is exactly what candidate 0 discusses.

The passage contains all three elements — Rav Huna's ruling (kosher), the conflicting Pumbedita tradition (tereifa), and the 'nahara nahara' response — and candidate 0's prose explicitly introduces this entire sequence as a unit returning to the dislocated leg question, while candidates 1 and 2 split the passage artificially across multiple headings.

Both items together form the continuous narrative of Rabbi Abba's encounter with Rav Yirmiya bar Abba — the challenge, the counter-appeal to the mishna, the apparent contradiction in Rav's rulings, the silence, and the proposed resolution — which is precisely what candidate 1 ('Rabbi Abba's inquiry') describes in its prose.

The passage contains Rabbi Abba's full recapitulation to Rabbi Zeira of everything that transpired in Babylonia — the direct questioning of Rav Huna, the encounter with Rabbi Yirmiya bar Abba, the contradiction within Rav's teachings, the dislocated vs. severed distinction, and Rav's explicit ruling — which is precisely what the 'Full recapitulation' prose describes as its content.

The passage directly discusses Rabbi Chanina's chicken with a dislocated thigh, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's ruling permitting it, and Rabbi Chanina's use of the preserved hen as a teaching tool — exactly what the 'Chanina's chicken' section's prose describes.

Both items together form the concluding halakhic ruling that overrides all preceding discussion — item 1 opens with 'the halakha is not in accordance with any of these statements' and item 2 completes the reasoning via the twelve-month principle — which matches heading 0 ('Widespread practice') whose prose explicitly states 'leis hilchasa k'chol hani shmaatsa — we do not rule in accordance with any of this entire preceding discussion.'
The passage describes Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta's empirical test of Rabbi Yehuda's down-feather ruling, which is precisely what the 'Down feather test' section's prose introduces and discusses.

The passage directly discusses the Gemara's challenge about whether Rabbi Yehuda holds that a tereifa can improve and the rebuttal that the very feature defining the tereifa status was restored superior to its original state, which is precisely what the 'Treifah improving' section's prose describes.
The passage describes Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥalafta's motivation to test the Proverbs verse about ants having no king, which is exactly what the 'Proverbs experiment' section's prose discusses.

The passage covers the entire experiment from spreading the cloak through tagging the scout ant and its report of shade — matching heading 0's prose about the summer setting, the cloak-as-shade, and the tagging of the scout — while heading 1 covers only the killing and the inference, which appear in later text not included here.
